correctness.rationale: Every fibre has 64 elements by the bilateral six-step linear recurrence. The four clopen phase classes of the period-doubling substitution make the normalized three-even-bit R-orbit a globally well-defined invariant. R has two fixed points and two three-cycles, so the candidate parts have fibre ranks 8,8,24,24. The exact residue-parity concatenation recurrence has matching states at levels two and six, yielding two valid subsequences of return permutations P and Q. Their quotient and the cube P^3 generate all odd-bit translations, proving the four complete fibre orbits algebraically. A reference bilateral base point returns under both subsequences; their return-fibre orbit transitivity and the established almost-periodicity theorem for permutative lifts imply the four invariant parts are minimal, distinct, and exhaustive. Standalone checker passed finite substitutions, 64-state group orbits, and independent direct cylinder returns at four lengths; these computations are not used to infer the infinite result.

originality.rationale: The novel claim is a precise component classification at the first non-dyadic even offset D=6 with unequal fibre ranks. The motivating September 2026 paper gives only nonminimality at odd block length seven and a general algorithmic framework. Two closest fully read published results treat D=2 (arbitrary modulus) or D=2^r >=4 (binary) and have equal ranks. Algebraic decomposition of 1+S^6 into smaller difference factors does not transfer these component counts because the intermediate base is no longer the period-doubling subshift. Exact period-four fibre holonomy and the four unequal-rank orbit classes are additional calculations not implied by those theorems. Targeted published-research semantic searches and public-literature alias queries did not locate exact coverage, but absent search hits are not proof of worldwide priority.

value.rationale: Offset six is the first even offset not covered by dyadic power-of-two calculations, a directly motivated boundary case for a natural family of period-doubling inverse images. The result shows unequal minimal-component fibre ranks in a complete compact binary symbolic model, in contrast to the uniform-rank outcomes of previously classified D=2 and D=2^r cases. It identifies the rank-splitting mechanism by an explicit order-three affine skeleton and full odd-coordinate holonomy, which is useful for understanding broader non-dyadic extensions; it is neither arbitrary finite slicing nor a numerical gain without structural reason.
